newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kobe Steel-TI venture completes expansion.
newsitem.headline: Kobe Steel-TI venture completes expansion.

text.p: KTI Semiconductor Ltd (KTI), a venture of Kobe Steel Ltd and Texas Instruments Inc (TI), said on Tuesday it had completed expansion of its chip-producing facility in Japan.
This will enable it to produce 64 megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips.
The expansion will enable KTI to more than double its production capacity to 25,000 semiconductor wafers per month, up from the current 10,000, KTI said in a statement.
"The eight-inch wafers are primarily for 16 megabit DRAMs but it will give KTI the capability to manufacture wafers for 64-megabit DRAM chips using 0.35-micron design rules," KTI said.
KTI is owned 75 percent by Kobe Steel and 25 percent by TI.
A Kobe Steel spokesman said it had not yet been decided when KTI would start producing 64-megabit DRAM chips.
"We will closely watch the market situation and decide when KTI will start making 64-megabit DRAM chips," he said.
